name: Fieldflow Calm acceptance and traceability contract

evidenceContract.rule: Every claim points to one hashed JSON evidence index bound to the requirement ID, verification method, exact implementation head and root-bound verification tuple matrix. A file hash alone is never evidence: typed reports, exhaustive tuple assertions, historical GitHub Actions provenance, Git ancestry, live GitHub review attestations and release deployment status are verified fail-closed. Free-text, sampled, manual, NOT_RUN, skipped and zero-proof claims never advance state.

indexSchema.reportCardinality: exactly one runtime report from MITIGATED or VERIFIED_LOCAL; exactly one staging report from VERIFIED_STAGING
indexSchema.trustedWorkflow: .github/workflows/fieldflow-calm-evidence.yml must have the same blob SHA-256 on PR base and evidence head

VERIFIED_LOCAL: typed requirement-bound commands passed with exitCode 0
machine-readable runtime report+sha256+all root-bound requirement/shared-matrix tuples executed exactly once+zero failures/skips/notRun
verified Git ancestry and successful GitHub Actions provenance
one live independent exact-HEAD APPROVED GitHub review
VERIFIED_STAGING: machine-readable staging report+sha256+all root-bound requirement/shared-matrix tuples executed exactly once+zero failures/skips/notRun

evidenceDimensions.rule: Every requirement declares its applicable density axis. The default is all three; a narrower set requires a reviewed scope decision. Compact never reduces rendered controls or pointer targets below 44px.

rule: No requirement may skip a state or be marked N/A. A scope change requires a separately reviewed manifest edit; missing fixtures, manual checks and NOT_RUN never count as evidence.

requirements.requirement: Prototypecommit, variant and reference hashes are immutable inputs to implementation; the complete contract digestvector is externally registered in the protected fieldflow-calm-contract environment and its base-owned pull_request_target status check is required before any lifecycle state advances.
All 75 dashboard pages and 4 authentication pages remain represented in routes.json.

Current loaders and Server Actions remain source authority for existing functionality and domain data. Their current unsafe or inconsistent behavior is explicitly superseded by contracted P0/P1 remediations, including FFC-PB-004, FFC-PB-010, FFC-PB-012 and FFC-PB-028; server-side tenant, permission, module and lifecycle enforcement remains authoritative at every write.
Rejected prototype variants and the design-lab switcher do not enter production.
A stale integration branch is synchronized with the current main branch before implementation work starts.
The package contains no unresolved placeholders and every contracted requirement maps to code, tests and runtime evidence before release.
Use the 4px spacing scale and named semantic spacing tokens from fieldflow-tokens.json.
Page sections use 30px rhythm, clusters 22px and panels 26px on canonical desktop.
Controls are 44px high and interactive targets are never below 44x44px.
Canonical panels use 22px radius, subtle line, inner highlight and premium shadow.
No text directly touches a border; internal padding is at least 12px and adjacent containers at least 16px apart.
Remove global class-name rewriting by tenant-admin-compact from the Fieldflow tree.
Tenant density scales named tokens, not arbitrary Tailwind class names, and retains accessibility minima.
Page gutters, max width, sidebar width, utility bar and heading geometry match the token manifest.
Buttons implement primary, secondary, quiet, outline, destructive and link variants with all interaction states.
All forms use canonical Label, Input, Select, Combobox, Checkbox, RadioGroup, Switch, Date/Time and validation composition.
Create/edit uses Sheet or step Dialog; destructive confirmation uses AlertDialog; native confirm/prompt/alert are absent.
Radix overlays trap and return focus, close with Escape where safe, lock scroll and use the shared z-index scale.
Tables use 50px headers and 74px comfortable rows; mobile uses deliberate cards rather than clipped tables.
Loading uses layout-preserving skeletons; empty, filtered-empty, error, forbidden and not-found states use the shared state system.
Motion uses the contracted durations and is removed or made instant under prefers-reduced-motion.
Resolve theme in order: code fallback, platform theme, legacy organization fallback, entitled tenant override.
Only entitled Enterprise tenants can activate tenant-specific branding; lower plans safely use platform defaults.

Existing brand, logo, favicon, splash, color, font, radius, density and email values are reused. The tenant-theme store adds only logo_mode/favicon_mode/splash_mode (inherit|asset|none) and monotone theme_revision; document-domain appearance snapshots required for immutable issued PDFs are separate lifecycle data, not duplicate editable visual values.
Theme variables are rendered server-side at a scope inherited by body-level Radix portals, without flash or hydration mismatch.

Tenant switch A→B replaces colors, fonts, assets, name, e-mail presentation and data from one appearanceSha256 bound to canonical host+tenantId+themeRevision+entitlement+override+presentation state, without stale cache or cross-tenant leakage.
Primary, secondary, accent, background, surface, text, muted and sidebar colors drive only their documented semantic tokens.
Success, warning, danger, info, locked and planboard category colors are stable semantic colors and cannot be overwritten by tenant branding.
Foreground colors are deterministically corrected to WCAG AA and settings explain any corrected low-contrast input.

Test dark, light, saturated red, bright yellow and monochrome brand profiles across controls, overlays and planboard. Planboard primary CTA, active view, selected work, links, focus and Now indicator consume tenant brand tokens; pastel categories and semantic conflict, locked and status meanings remain fixed.
Tenant fonts are actually applied to body and headings on tenant backoffice, auth and customer/personnel portal surfaces; canonical responsive geometry survives font metric differences.
Radius and density presets are applied through shared tokens on every backoffice/auth page, customer/personnel portal shell and portal overlay.
Missing, broken and very wide logos plus long tenant names preserve header/sidebar/auth and customer/personnel portal geometry at every responsive evidence width.

Full whitelabel removes tenant-facing Fieldgrid wordmarks and copy from shell, login, metadata, favicon, manifest, email, PDF, customer/personnel web portals and PWA install surfaces where contractually enabled. The published public website is excluded from this claim; WebsiteTheme remains its separately versioned authority.
Platform/support/audit identity remains internally attributable while tenant-facing presentation stays whitelabel.
Asset uploads remain tenant-scoped, server-validated, type/size-limited and reject unsanitized SVG.
Brand settings provide desktop/mobile preview, reset to effective platform theme, upload progress and explicit asset errors.
Static root metadata and favicon are replaced with host-aware resolved metadata for tenant-facing routes.
Whitelabel regression search covers shell copy, planning copy, organization placeholders, email templates, PDFs and portals.

Public website branding remains a separately versioned publication contract. Capacitor web content, safe-area canvas and runtime StatusBar background/style activate atomically from one integrity-checked host+tenant+revision theme snapshot. Invalid activation keeps the last safe effective theme; cold start, corrupt cache, stale revision or hash mismatch falls atomically back to the hashed safe platform theme without leaking another tenant. Native Android launcher name, package, icon, OS splash and build-time notification/channel assets remain explicitly outside the runtime whitelabel claim.
runtimeCases: light theme resolves contrast-safe runtime chrome
dark theme resolves contrast-safe runtime chrome
low-contrast candidate is rejected without replacing the last safe effective theme
cold start uses the hashed safe platform theme until a verified snapshot resolves
corrupt cache, stale revision or hash mismatch falls back atomically to the hashed safe platform theme
host+tenant+revision cache isolation passes tenant A to tenant B to tenant A without cross-tenant paint
Capacitor StatusBar background, icon style and safe-area canvas switch as one atomic transition
plugin-mock and Android emulator evidence record the same resolved native runtime tuple

requirements.requirement: Brand assets upload exactly once and activate atomically with a version-safe theme save. logo_mode/favicon_mode/splash_mode represent inherit|asset|none without URL/path inference; theme_revision increments once per effective change; failure preserves the previous appearance and orphan cleanup is controlled.
Fieldflow uses a 228px sidebar from 861 through 1460px and 252px above 1460px; the mobile/tablet shell through 860px uses an accessible modal navigation drawer.
Shell height uses dynamic viewport units and safe-area insets where applicable; no viewport is trapped by h-screen behavior.
Navigation derives from the canonical route registry, permissions and module entitlements.
Settings overview and tabs expose exactly the same permission-filtered sections, including Branding, Qualifications and Product Experience.
Website tabs are filtered by granular website permissions; direct URLs remain server-guarded.
Global search, notifications, tenant switcher, profile and support context stay reachable at every viewport.
Support mode is unmistakable, tenant context is visible and mutations retain server-side support/audit context.
Skip link targets the main region and focus lands predictably after navigation.
Sidebar groups use task-led labels while support routes remain discoverable and no current route is orphaned.
Production contains only Fieldflow Calm, not the prototype design switcher or explanatory lab chrome.
Every production-inventory.json entry retains every existingProduction capability and action with its exact permission, module, feature, plan and tenant-setting gates.
Primary action is singular and visible; secondary row/page actions live in predictable menus; destructive actions are separated.
Assignments, customers, objects and personnel use one shared responsive data-view pattern.
Materials and inventory replace min-width-only tables with the same responsive data-view/card pattern.
Customer, object, assignment and personnel dossiers share hero, status strip, responsive section navigation and action rail/sheet.

Every list preserves exactly the search, filters, sorting, pagination, view preferences, selection, bulk and export capabilities recorded for that route in production-inventory.json; absent capabilities are not invented.
Every mutation exposes only the specific action allowed by its server permission, not a bundled canWrite approximation.
Roles UI uses the tenant role tables and actions read by runtime authorization; legacy global roles are not presented as effective tenant permissions.
Existing fine-grained delete/archive/manage permissions and their Server Actions are reconciled and tested per action.
No hidden tab or unreachable component is counted as delivered functionality.
Website page editor uses a responsive three-pane studio with drawer/sheet adaptations while preserving revision-safe actions.
Authentication and first-run use effective host branding and complete validation, pending, success and failure states.

Planning exposes working board, day, week, month and map modes through canonical view/date query parameters. Switching modes preserves every applicable date, search, filter and display value, while legacy day/week/month parameters normalize without losing state.

Board and day timeline modes render hours horizontally and employees vertically, with sticky time header and staff column. Phone defaults to the agenda; its optional timeline preserves these axes inside one labelled local scroll region.
Pastel blocks preserve semantic labels/icons and contrast; color is not the only state signal.

One pure shared placement engine governs indicative client preview and server evaluation for 15-minute snap, bounds, pointer offset, overlap and movable status. New queue placement uses the canonical estimated duration clamped to 30–480 minutes; an existing block preserves its exact valid duration with a 15-minute minimum. Immediately before the atomic write, the Server Action independently reloads tenant-scoped state and authoritatively validates permission, module, lifecycle/status, fresh assignment/staffing versions, sickness/leave/availability, role, sector, certificate, diploma, knowledge, region, duplicate staffing, required slots and capacity. A blocker writes nothing; a warning requires explicit confirmation.
Fieldflow raster is 15 minutes in client and server; the existing 90-minute planningTimeSlotMinutes default is not silently repurposed as grid snap.
Pointer offset inside an existing block is retained during drag.

Queue→board, board→board and explicit board→queue workflows are complete. Board and day also expose the full New assignment wizard on desktop and mobile; its UI availability follows assignments:write unless one reviewed server policy atomically aligns UI and action authorization.

Board→queue distinguishes unassigning one employee from releasing the whole assignment and previews team impact. Unassign removes one active staffing link and preserves team timing; whole release is pre-start only, atomically removes every active staffing link, transitions scheduled to plannable, clears scheduledDate/start/end, records a complete audited before snapshot and never changes actual timestamps. Both paths support version-safe full undo.
Only plannable and scheduled assignments are movable; UI and server use one status helper.
A normal drop changes exactly the selected planning intent and never silently shifts another assignment or unassigns staff.
Automatic conflict resolution is offered only as a separate previewed, atomic and completely undoable action; a normal drop never invokes it.
Every mutation sends client-observed assignment and staffing versions and fails closed on stale data.

Mutation IDs are durable and idempotent and responses cannot overwrite newer local or server state. One tenant+actor+mutationId receipt stores request hash, status, complete saved result and affected before/after version sets in the same transaction as the domain write; exact replay returns the receipt and a reused ID with a different payload fails closed across retries and restarts.
Optimistic placement immediately moves the card with pending state; error restores the exact prior snapshot.

Undo covers queue placement, interest selection, moves, employee changes, unassignment, release and explicit optimization. The mutation stores complete before/after record sets and assignment/staffing/interest-response version maps; undo verifies every after-version and restores the entire set with fresh monotone lifecycle versions atomically or writes nothing after any newer change.

Backoffice consumes tenant-scoped planning_refresh through the existing management realtime channel and adds planboard-specific coordination. Every event carries server-derived tenantId/actorUserId, mutationId, monotone revision and originClientId; the subscriber rejects another tenant, deduplicates by tenantId+revision, retains a per-tenant high-water mark, coalesces and defers during drag, wizard or pending mutation, then fetches until the applied revision reaches that high-water mark and exposes degraded/stale status when needed.

Outside an active interaction, a committed change is visible in a second planner within at most 2000 ms measured from the receipt linearization timestamp; outbox dispatch, channel delivery and catch-up retries share that hard budget.
Scheduled and actual timestamps remain separate and all operational views use resolveAssignmentEffectiveInterval in Europe/Amsterdam.
Running blocks render actual start→now; completed blocks render actual start→end; planned outline remains visible.
Midnight and both DST transitions are tested with one shared Amsterdam clock/date helper.
Required staffing uses resolveRequiredSlots everywhere and team timing impact is shown before confirmation.

Interest selection atomically confirms the selected response and assigns that personnel member. It reconciles requiredSlots as max(explicit required personnel count, distinct required role count, 1), recomputes filledSlots from distinct active assigned personnel, and transitions to scheduled only when the complete planned moment exists and every required slot is filled. It never regresses an active or final workflow status, preserves planned fields when work starts or completes, and emits one deduplicated refresh.
Mobile supports plan, exact time, move, replace employee, unassign/release, conflict review, confirm, cancel and undo without drag.
Keyboard supports select, raster/hour movement, employee change, confirm and cancel with aria-live feedback.
Queue supports search and all/best-match/urgent filters; employees sort by best/name/load/region.
Week is a real seven-day employee capacity view with planned/available hours, occupancy, attention and day drilldown.

Month uses real aggregates, accessible overflow details and a week link that opens the actual week view. At 320, 390 and 430px it is list/agenda-first and never presents a compressed seven-column calendar as the primary interface.
Map preserves real Google Maps, routes, ETA, travel mode, warnings and fallback list; time suggestions use the shared mutation engine.

Map mode is shown only when the shared server gate confirms the map feature flag, required Google Maps configuration, enabled planning module and planning:read permission. Route calculation and time application repeat that gate server-side; time application additionally requires planning:write.
Planboard remains usable at 1920px, 200% zoom and production-scale employee/block counts without page-level horizontal overflow.
Every route is proven at 320, 390, 430, 768, 1024, 1280, 1440 and 1920 pixels.
No route has document-level horizontal overflow; controlled planboard/table subregions are explicitly labelled and keyboard-scrollable.
Forms are one column on phones; two columns only when every field remains at least 280px wide.
Tables become prioritized mobile cards with identity, status, up to three metadata lines and action menu.
Dossier tabs scroll accessibly or become a labelled selector; content for inactive tabs is not exposed to assistive technology.
Settings index changes from sticky rail to horizontal index and then drawer/select without hiding sections.
Long Dutch labels, validation messages, names, addresses and amounts wrap without overlap or truncating critical meaning.
Browser zoom at 200% preserves content, actions and reflow without two-dimensional page scrolling.
On-screen keyboards and safe areas do not obscure sheet/dialog actions on phone.
At wide widths content remains max-width bounded and readable while the planboard can use additional horizontal time space.
WCAG 2.2 AA is the release baseline; automated Axe has no serious or critical violation.
Every interactive control is keyboard reachable with visible focus and logical order.
Icon-only controls have accessible names and tooltips are supplementary, never the sole label.
Status, priority, conflict, locked and validation states use text/icon in addition to color.
Field errors are associated with controls, summarized when appropriate and announced after submit.
Dialogs, sheets, menus, popovers, comboboxes, tabs and alerts use canonical Radix/shadcn semantics.
Async mutations announce pending, success, error and rollback without moving focus unexpectedly.
Charts, capacity visuals and pastel planboard blocks expose equivalent names/values in text.
Reduced motion, forced colors/high contrast and text spacing overrides preserve operation.
Touch targets remain at least 44px under every density, viewport and theme.
Every route and mutation rechecks tenant, permission and entitlement on the server.
Direct URL and forged action calls are denied even when a control is hidden.
Two-tenant tests prove no data, asset, theme, event, cache or search-context leakage.
Roles and user administration are reconciled to canonical tenant-role tables used by runtime authorization.

If live legacy role bindings require reconciliation, it is a separate reviewed W10 data migration with audit, backup and rollback; it is never folded into the W01 appearance migration or a UI-only implementation PR.
Secrets and restricted dossier/security content never appear in client payloads or DOM without read permission.
File uploads retain tenant-scoped paths, MIME/size validation, malware policy and authorized downloads.
Support mode mutations retain grant, TTL, reason and audit context and cannot escape the selected tenant.

Effective deployed grants and RLS policies for organization_settings and tenant_domains are fail-closed and tenant-scoped; historical permissive policies are removed by a reviewed forward migration when present.
Branding storage write and delete policies bind the authenticated actor and object path to the same tenant; forged cross-tenant asset IDs, URLs and paths are rejected.
Email, PWA and PDF branding consume owned or explicitly allowlisted assets; PDF image resolution blocks private addresses, unsafe redirects and DNS rebinding to prevent SSRF.
Custom domains require real DNS and TLS verification, canonical primary-host routing and tested callback, cookie, CSP, CORS and trusted-proxy behavior before activation.
Theme settings, active asset references and audit evidence commit atomically or through a recoverable outbox so a reported failure cannot leave an unaudited active theme.
Fieldflow is selected server-side with a fail-closed experience flag after tenant resolution.
Legacy and Fieldflow share loaders, actions and domain helpers; business logic is not forked.
Legacy stays the global default until full route, role, state, theme and viewport evidence is complete.
The strict Fieldflow visual gate fails on missing fixtures, zero screenshots, manual status, missing baseline or uncovered route/action/state.
Canonical 1440 CI screenshots use fixed browser, fonts and fixtures; meaningful geometry differs by at most 1px and unmasked pixel difference stays below the reviewed threshold.
Only timestamps/current-time line and nondeterministic third-party map tiles may be narrowly masked; masks never cover controls or layout.
Every implementation PR reports exact base/head, routes, actions, permissions, theme cases, commands, evidence and rollback.
No implementation PR merges with open P0/P1 findings, unresolved placeholders, console errors, hydration errors or failed gates.
Independent functional/security and visual/a11y reviews are recorded before main promotion.
Pilot starts with fixed test tenants on staging, then allowlist, then global default; each step has sign-off.
Rollback is configuration-only to legacy plus deployment of the recorded previous good SHA if needed; no database rollback is expected.
Exact-head promotion follows feature→UIUX master→main→staging; no direct staging or main commit is used.

Dashboard, list, dossier, form, settings and wizard page families use the shared Fieldflow composition harness with identical loading, empty, filtered-empty, validation, pending, success, error and forbidden semantics where applicable.
Quotes, reports and invoices retain their complete create, review, approve, issue, payment, download and immutable document-snapshot workflows with action-level permissions and responsive evidence.

Cross-work-package integration proves legacy-flag-off parity, Fieldflow-flag-on parity, deep links, shared loaders/actions, API compatibility and absence of duplicated business logic before staging promotion.
Materials, inventory, assignment/personnel inventory context, documents and checklist routes preserve their route-specific production inventory and action gates in responsive Fieldflow compositions.
Tickets, news, website, help, roadmap and release routes preserve their exact production inventory, conditional actions, module gates and tenant settings without adding unsupported controls.
Planning and smart-planning settings share the approved placement/matching invariants while preserving their distinct production actions, permissions and per-sector rule saves/resets.

Dashboard, assignment, customer, object and personnel routes preserve their exact production inventory—including the limited pending-leave inbox—while adopting shared Fieldflow list, dossier and responsive compositions.
